hyps.why: Edge 1 reaches the output only through edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the upgrade affects a dead path and gains almost nothing.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, which reaches the output only via edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the edit has no effect.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which receives input only through edge 0, so with edge 0 removed the edit is on a dead path.
Edge 4 starts at node 1, which is cut off from the input when edge 0 is none, so upgrading it yields no gain.
Replacing a parameter-free pooling op with a 3x3 conv gains less than replacing a 1x1 conv (about 2.3, 3.6 and 3.7 points versus 3.3, 4.7 and 8.6).
The direct input-to-output edge is already a useful skip path, so replacing it with a 3x3 conv gains much less than replacing a 1x1 conv.
When the direct 0->3 skip path is present, extra conv capacity on edge 4 is partly redundant and the gain shrinks.
Upgrading from pooling gives a smaller gain than upgrading from a 1x1 conv, especially on ImageNet16-120 (3.1 versus 8.1).
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip loses a lot of capacity, so it hurts far more than replacing a 1x1 conv.
Replacing pooling with a conv gives a smaller gain (1.5, 3.0 and 3.5 points) than replacing a 1x1 conv (2.6, 4.4 and 8.0).
